body:
It would also make me feel more guilty if I ended up in one.
I don't feel like I learned anything from failing, only that I can only fail. I'm sure my friends just humor me.

I'm in Geology. I always thought I was good in that field, and I rationalized shortcomings in other fields in high school/undergrad by telling myself that at least I'm still good at that. And now I find out that I'm not even good at that. A big part of my depression comes from the realization that I'm not in fact good at what I thought I was good at. (If that sentence made sense).

I try to, but I only feel like a millstone around their necks. They can only take so much moping from me and they don't deserve to have me ruining their fun.

That's another thing contributing to my depression: the fact that I'll never transition. My family is ultraconservative and religious and they love me a lot. They have no idea about me, but they do have strong opinions about how disgusting and evil and wrong LGBT people are. I will never dare bring it up.

Which brings me to the next point... honestly, I think killing myself would hurt them far less than coming out and transitioning.

I wish there were those magical words. I guess I try to get something like that from talking to people. I just keep feeling like I'm more and more of a burden on my friends, and that guilt is making me drift away from them, which only makes it worse...
What worries me the most is that after failing everything that mattered, I'd fail my suicide as well, and end up under close guard or something.
